pt.title: Competente o Suficiente
pt.subtitle: Um ano colocando a inteligência artificial à prova, sem medo e sem propaganda.
pt.alt: Competente o Suficiente as a 3D paperback: a giant retro-futurist robot with a weary round face kneels at a 1950s World's Fair while a crowd watches. The title runs down the navy spine.

intro: I took the year's articles from my blog, reorganized and rewrote them as one story, fact-checked them again and illustrated them. It's for anyone anxious or confused about AI: the professional afraid of being replaced, the parent who read that AGI is two years away, the manager being sold an "AI transformation".

inside.title: What's inside
inside.lede: Five parts, each answering a question people keep asking me about AI.

inside.extras: Plus two interludes and ten appendices, from how the machine works inside (no math) and three bubbles, dot-com to AI, to studying with AI at your side, a safety kit for agents, the behind-the-scenes for programmers and whether this book was written by AI.

made.title: Making-of
made.lede: How 131 blog posts, almost half a million words, became one book written with agents, without losing control of what it says.
points: Every post went into a sealed inventory with a hash, and a lineage map says which post superseded which, so the book tells the latest state of what I measured.
Every paragraph carries an invisible marker of the post it came from. When I edit a post, one command lists the paragraphs to review.
Every number, date and name was checked against the posts, the reference projects and primary sources. Some of the corrections were to my own blog.
Agents wrote the drafts. Reading, cutting, correcting and approving every chapter stayed with me.
made.quote: The agents were competent enough to write the draft. Deciding what it said remained my job.
made.quoteOriginal: Os agentes foram competentes o suficiente pra escrever o rascunho. Decidir o que ele dizia continuou sendo trabalho meu.
